items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1961-06-28
items.q: But the next following week, Hunts and Nagels then got Joe Oliver's whole band over there.

ctx.x: We got him up in Baton Rouge, remember Ralph?

Yeah. And, uh, Eddie Atkins was playing trombone. Oh, yeah. Eddie Atkins. And, uh, let's see, Joe, Joe was on the trumpet. And, uh, let's see, Ed. Uh, clarinet, let's see who. He had a clarinet, uh, C. Now he had, uh, Willie, Willie Caput, uh, Chris Minor, and Pop Foster. And he had a clarinet, I think. Uh, uh, I don't know if he was just for his name now. Uh, Lorenzo Teale. and he had a clarinet Lorenzo Teal Lorenzo Teal
Did they have any name for the band? Is it Joe's band? Magnolia band

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1961-06-28
items.q: Interviewee describes King Oliver's habit of throwing a brick to signal the end of a set, but does not claim personal interaction or direct association.

ctx.x: 325 North Johnson and this is Bill Russell and Ralph Collins is here and the date is June the 28th, 1961. Well, I think I would have, Dick Allen just stopped by and I said what can we ask Mr. Dawson? He said ask about the time that the King Oliver used to drop the brick or something.

What was that for? That was for the, to give you a notice to stop playing, you know. When you, the boys when they knock off, they keep on playing over, you know, couple of strings, couple of bars over the beat, over the knockoff and well, he just got a big brick and when he got ready to knock off he throw the brick down on the music stand and see I guess you'll hear that. He really did that, huh? Yeah, he did that. I don't think he was kissing. No, no, he did that, yeah.

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1972-04-05
items.q: when I was playing with, uh, with, uh, what you call him, uh, Joe Oliver, we playing at Hunts and Nagel on Ray's.

ctx.x: They used to have your small band. Yeah.

Uh, well, you see, uh, they used to dance. They had, uh, they sell liquor there, you know, they had women working there, uh, hustling. And, uh, the fellas, people would come in there. Most of the men from off the ships, they'd come in there and spend money and dance. And go on and have a good time and put, uh, we had a kiddie box that we, that dropped the money in the kiddie box for the different numbers that they want to hear, you see. And, uh, now, uh, T-Net played, uh, the last I heard of him, he played with…

What about Abadese? Did you ever go by Abadese? Down there, I figured it was on the anvil. Well, it had another name and I can't remember. Something like the, the Princeton Inn or the Princeton Club or something like that. No, Joe Oliver used to be there with Big Eye Louie and Ernest Rogers and Wooden Joe was in there playing clarinet. Yeah. You know the place. That was the Magnolia band. No, I think Richard M. Jones was there. Not the Magnolia. Not the band that was on Hunts and Nagels, but another one. This is…

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1962-01-31
items.q: Joe Oliver got with Joe Oliver. And him and Joe Oliver formed a band with Chicago. And they worked together with two of them in the same band until they fell out.

ctx.x: Well, uh, they'd have six pieces. We went to the Junk Hotel and played there. Well, he had Son Thomas playing guitar. I was playing bass. He had, uh, Dominic Remy on the trumpet. They had two trumpets. He had T-Boy Remy with him. And he had a fella called Pill on the clarinet. He died. He had a little bow-legged fella called Pill. Well, after that, well, Louis played around spot jobs around different places. And then, that's when he went up the line. Joe Oliver got with Joe Oliver. And him and Joe Oliver formed a…
And, uh, did he have a trombone down here, Louis? Used the trombone much?
